_what: Batygin & Brown (2016)'s luck test reproduced: the six objects beyond 250 AU against 100,000 draws of six from every object with q > 30 AU and a > 50 AU first seen before 2016, as the paper drew, by the spread of their closest points on the sky and of the lines their orbits tilt about; the same draws on to a million to count those tight in both (joint_check); the same on today's catalogue. Computed by scripts/build_bb2016.py; see its header for the method.
_src: orbits: JPL Small-Body Database (the team's download) and etnos.json; discovery dates: MPC NumberedMPs.txt

closest.src: Batygin & Brown 2016, section 2: 'Orbits as tightly clustered in perihelion position as the 6 observed KBOs occur only 0.7% of the time'

tilt.src: Batygin & Brown 2016, section 2: 'a cluster as tight as that observed in the data occurs only 1% of the time'

both.src: Batygin & Brown 2016, abstract and section 2: 'only 0.007%', 'about 3.8 sigma'

draws.src: Batygin & Brown 2016, section 2: 'We then randomly select 6 objects from the sample 100,000 times'
